headline: Nasdaq-100 retraces from its session high as semiconductors lag and the 30-year holds 5.64% into the final Q3 close
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30512.82, up 173.49 points or 0.57%, after printing a session high of 30630.45 and opening at 30421.68 against a 30415.16 low. The index has since given back about 118 points from that high, so the earlier advance met a genuine retracement rather than extending in a straight line. That is the single most important observation for path risk: mean reversion is functioning intraday, which is why Tail stays at 22 in the watch band rather than pushing toward the 25 block threshold. Confirmation is absent. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is at 12580.57, down 0.38% and close to its 12555.65 session low after an earlier 12731.10 high, so the sector that normally leads a Nasdaq-100 advance sits near the bottom of its range while the index sits in the upper half of its own. The Dow is modestly lower while the Nasdaq Composite is up around 1%, a narrow advance concentrated in large-cap technology. Under the standing contract that conflict reduces directional conviction and raises Stress; it does not mechanically raise Tail. Rates are the dominant stress input. The 10-year yield is 5.30% at the top of its 5.20-5.30 daily range and the highest since April 2002, and the 30-year is 5.64% at its session high and the highest since June 2002, against a 2-year near 4.92% on the September 28 H.15 daily figures. That is a bear steepening, and notably it is occurring even as October rate-hike odds fell to roughly 37% from about 51% a day earlier after August core PCE printed 0.2% month-on-month against 0.3% expected, with the year-on-year rate steady at 3.0%. Front-end relief alongside long-end pressure points to term premium rather than policy expectations, which is a persistent stress condition rather than a price-path mechanism. Volatility is decaying. VIX is 15.84, down 1.25% and below its 16.32 session high, which does not corroborate an imminent pathological path. WTI is $90.96, up 1.77%, rebounding from the prior session's fall as Strait of Hormuz disruption concerns are weighed against Middle East export recovery; oil is supportive of Stress but shows no equity transmission today. Two scheduled structures define the remainder of the US session. The 19:00Z-21:00Z span combines the power hour and cash close on the final session of Q3, where market-on-close imbalances can impose flow that is not price discovery, with the Micron fiscal Q4 report scheduled just after the close into thinning liquidity. Those overlap into the published danger window at Tail 24, which remains a conditional flow and catalyst checkpoint rather than observed structure. Shared Finviz context was read and rejected as an evidence input: its latest publication is dated 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly 18 hours old and well outside the 90-minute freshness window, with collectionStatus partial and both the futures and calendar sections unavailable. This assessment therefore rests entirely on independently verified current sources.

lookbackSummary: Published Claude assessments across the preceding 24 hours held Tail between 15 and 23. The mapping was green EA_ON from the 20:00Z hour of September 29 through the Asian and European hours of September 30, with Stress easing from the mid-70s to about 65 overnight. The state returned to the watch band from the 12:00Z hour as the US pre-open and the August PCE release approached, and Tail then firmed through the cash session to 22 in the 14:00Z hour and 23 in the 15:00Z and 16:00Z hours as long-end yields reversed higher.
outlookSummary: Tail holds at 22 in the current hour and through the post-Chicago-PMI digestion hour, then widens to 24 across 19:00Z-21:00Z where the quarter-end power hour, the final Q3 cash close and the scheduled Micron fiscal Q4 release overlap. It eases through late-US digestion, returns to the low band from the 23:00Z hour and reaches its floor at 16 in the quietest late-Asian stretch, before firming again through the European session of October 1 and into the 12:30Z jobless claims release, the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:00Z ISM Manufacturing print, which peaks the second half of the window at 24 before easing to 22. No forecast hour reaches the 25 block threshold. September payrolls on October 2 falls beyond this window.
